source_text: fidem, quia nullum adulterium; prolem, ipsum Dominum Christum; sacramentum, quia nullum divortium quia concubitus defuit, nullo modo fuisse coniugium
pass_a_gloss: Faith, because no adulterium; prolem, itself Lord Christ; sacrament, because no divortium because concubitus defuit, by-no now/only to-have-been marriage.
pass_b_english: Augustine reports that Julian argued that, because intercourse was absent, Mary and Joseph’s relationship was not a marriage.
Whatever was otherwise would seem evil.

choices.why: Opening fides promissionis is the pledge of a promise, not the theological virtue.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded. This row is Augustine's report; Pass A glosses only the Julian words recoverable here.
